dedupe_keys.name: edgar food global emission inventory of food systems

description: EDGAR-FOOD is a global inventory of greenhouse gas and air pollutant emissions from food systems, split by the stage of the food life cycle: production including land use change, processing, packaging, transport, retail, consumption and end of life, and by the economic sector that emits (land-based, energy, industry and waste). It shows that food systems account for about a third of human greenhouse gas emissions. The producer is the European Commission Joint Research Centre's EDGAR team (Monica Crippa and colleagues), described in Nature Food in 2021 and 2022. Coverage is every country, annually: greenhouse gases 1990–2023 in the 2025 release and air pollutants 1990–2018. Data are Excel workbooks downloadable without registration; the site asks users to follow its conditions of use and cite the papers, and no licence is named on the pages read. Caveats: stage shares rest on modelled allocations of energy and industrial emissions, the latest year is an estimate, and releases built on different EDGAR versions are not directly comparable. Simulation uses: emissions of cold chains, food transport, retail and food waste disposal for climate adaptation and mitigation scenarios of food supply infrastructure. Related records: the What a Waste global database (data-what-a-waste-global-database) covers waste generation.
